description: We are Team Galactic geeks, a group of 4 students from KLE College Belagavi. Our team combines strength in data analysis and full-stack development. We're working on the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge, building a tool that turns NASA satellite data into practical recommendations for farmers in North Karnataka
summary: Field Shift helps farmers in Belagavi district decide what to grow next. A farmer enters the taluk, soil, season, last crop, irrigation and what matters most to them. That could be soil health, saving water or a safe harvest. The tool gives each crop a score based on rotation, soil, climate and water use. It then compares three options, the usual crop and the two best others, and shows if the best choice would change when a water need we are not sure about turns out to be different. We use NASA POWER daily data from 1981 to 2025. It is a model estimate, so we only use it to compare zones and years. In dry Athani, a dry spell of seven or more days in July and August happened in 38 of 45 years, while wet Khanapur and Belagavi had far fewer. The tool works in Kannada and English. It supports the farmer and the local agriculture officer and it never replaces them. We show warnings, equal choices and uncertainty openly instead of hiding them.
details:
Farmers in Belagavi district must choose what to grow next while rain,
heat and water are changing, and a farmer in wet Khanapur should not
get the same advice as a farmer in dry Athani. Field Shift is a
decision-support tool that helps a farmer compare rotation choices.
The farmer enters taluk, soil, season, last crop, irrigation, and what
matters most: soil health, saving water, a safe harvest, or balanced.
The tool scores every crop on four things, rotation, soil, climate
and water use, shows the best crops, and compares three strategies:
the usual crop and the two best others, each with why, evidence,
benefits, information gaps and risks. It then runs a stability check:
does the best choice stay the same if the unconfirmed water needs are
lower or higher than assumed? For example, in Athani in rabi, after
soybean, saving water, chickpea and rabi jowar tie at 10, with wheat
at 9; if the water need is lower, chickpea wins alone, if higher,
rabi jowar wins alone.

It is a clear point-scoring system, not machine learning. All weights
and thresholds sit in one settings block in scoring.py, and the
Streamlit app only calls scoring.py; it never changes a number or a
weight. We built it with Python, Streamlit and pandas, and tested it
with 4 fixed test cases in check_tests.py, all passing.

The evidence comes from NASA POWER daily data, 1981–2025, at Belagavi,
Khanapur and Athani. NASA POWER is a model estimate, so we use it only
to compare zones and years, never for exact rainfall. It shows a dry
spell of 7 or more days in July–August in 38 of 45 years in Athani,
against 12 in Belagavi and 10 in Khanapur, and low stored soil moisture
on 1 October in 38 of 45 years in Athani, against 9 in each of the
other two zones. All three zones warm by about 0.11 to 0.13 °C per
decade. Rotation pairs come from UAS Dharwad and ICAR sources for black
soil, which list common systems, not Belagavi-specific advice. Dr. D. A.
Mhetre, Senior Scientist and Head, ICAR-BIRDS KVK Tukkanatti, Belagavi,
was consulted through a team member on 22 and 31 October 2026, with a
follow-up on 2 November 2026. He allowed us to use his name and
suggested corrections, including sugarcane-based cropping and rotation
after sugarcane. His two answers on water order were not fully
consistent, so we did not use his water order for the scores.

The benefit is a farmer-friendly tool in Kannada and English that a
farmer can discuss with an expert, instead of following a black-box
answer. Its creative strength is honesty: warnings, equal choices and
the stability check are shown, never hidden. We considered farmer
priorities, soil, season, previous crop, irrigation, and what we do
not know. Stated openly: water need of chickpea, green gram and black
gram is unconfirmed; pigeon pea, mixed cropping and sugarcane are not
in the tool yet; there are no sourced rotations for red soil or for
rabi followed by kharif; there are no yield, price or profit numbers;
Kannada was checked by a Kannada-speaking team member, not an
independent reviewer; the taluk-to-zone map comes from a 2011 CRIDA
plan, listing 10 taluks while the district may have 15; and there are
no verified Belagavi farmer interviews yet. Testing with Belagavi
farmers is a next step.
dataRefs: NASA POWER — daily data, 1981–2025 (rainfall, temperature, root-zone soil wetness)
